turns.content: For a common four-bit suffix b3b2b1b0 in base 2 and base 5, with leading zeros allowed, define its numerical values x and y in the two bases and express n as congruences modulo 16 and 625.
Use the Chinese remainder theorem to determine how many n in 0<=n<10000 correspond to each permitted suffix, and decide whether matching digits make x and y numerically equal.
As a sanity check, compare x and y for a nontrivial suffix such as 1000 and explain the difference.
Derive the residue formula for each solution class using the two quantities introduced above and the required modulus.
Take the suffixes to be b3b2b1n and sum x and y over them.
Use the formula and those two sums to find the requested aggregate modulo the stated modulus.
